## HueMux v0.0.2-alpha.15 — Files you can actually find

> **Alpha.** Fixes the two file-handling problems from alpha.14.

### The diagnostics button downloaded nothing

My fault, introduced in alpha.13. The button used to navigate the page to the
diagnostics endpoint, which worked because Android's WebView intercepts a
navigation that carries a download header. alpha.13 moved that navigation into
a hidden iframe — to stop a failed download replacing the Settings page with a
wall of text — and the interception does not happen for an iframe. The safety
measure removed the only thing that made the button work.

Files no longer go through a navigation at all. The page fetches the text over
loopback, which always works, and the app writes it to **Downloads**. You get
the resulting path on screen, and a **Share** button to send it somewhere.

### "It recorded, but where did it go?"

Recording reported a filename and left the folder implicit. Both recorders now
report the location they actually resolved, the sync page shows it verbatim,
and a **Share** button opens the system share sheet for the file.

So: no save dialog, but the file's location is stated and one tap sends it
anywhere. If you would rather pick the destination yourself before recording,
say so and I will add a save dialog — it needs the recording start to become
asynchronous, which is why it is not in this build.

Recordings still go to Movies/HueMux. If alpha.14's recording worked and you
could not find the file, it was almost certainly there.

### Also

A hash change on an already-open app did nothing — `#settings` on a loaded page
is a same-document navigation, so the tab stayed put while the address bar
claimed otherwise. That also affected the Back button after a tab switch.

### What is verified

Browser-side: the redirect resolves a direct page load to the right tab, hash
changes switch tabs both ways, the download produces a real file with the
Settings page intact, and the Share button stays hidden where there is no app
to share through.

Not verified: everything Android-specific. This machine has no Android SDK, so
the write to Downloads and the share sheet are compiled for the first time by
CI and run for the first time by you.
